label: At D1, higher after a rewarded last trial, lower after choosing a2 or reaching S1.
terms: (phase == D1) * in_rew ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * in_rew * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * ep_dec * (prev_action == 2)
explanation: Raw reset gate r36 is large mainly at D1 and rises through the episode (timing R^2 0.79). Beyond timing, the D1 value is set by the previous trial roughly additively: about +0.18 if it was rewarded, -0.14 if the choice was a2, -0.13 if the reached state was S1. So it is highest after a1->S2 rewarded (rare-rewarded) and lowest after a2->S1 unrewarded. The free fit adds a super-additive a1 S2 rewarded interaction, a small belief_lo term and a small GO-phase a1 effect (dev 0.64 vs 0.52 for the short form). The trial before last and episode-scaled terms add almost nothing. GO and D2 residuals are small. Uses observed variables only.

issues: The directions in the label are right. The recorded short form scores test 0.517 beyond timing (dev 0.515), with weights reward +0.184, a2 -0.142, S1 -0.133. But the additive last-trial table alone reaches 0.68, so the short form leaves a lot unexplained.

Systematic miss 1 (misses on the recorded short form): at D1 the model under-predicts after a1->S2 by +0.189 when rewarded and +0.148 when not. This is an a1-and-S2 boost on top of the separate effects, and it holds whether or not the trial was rewarded. The explanation calls the extra boost reward-specific ('when a1->S2 was rewarded'), which is not supported. The profile residuals are a1S2r +0.37 and a1S2u +0.145 against a1S1r +0.08 and a2S2r +0.06, so the a1-vs-a2 gap is about 0.30 given S2 but only about 0.12-0.18 given S1.

Systematic miss 2: the model over-predicts D1 after '?' by -0.119. '?' is the window's first trial, where prev_action and prev_state are -1. The terms (prev_action==2) and (prev_state==1) are both 0 there, so these steps get the a1->S2 level, the highest one. This is a coding artifact, and it alone costs about 0.08 test R^2.

A better short form fixes both the coding and the artifact: (phase==D1)*prev_reward ;; (phase==D1)*(prev_action - prev_state) ;; (phase==D1)*(prev_action > 0). It scores test 0.600 and dev 0.606, against 0.517 for the recorded form. Weights: +0.150 for reward, -0.226 for (a - s), -0.083 for having a previous trial. So a1->S2 is about +0.23, a2->S1 about -0.23, and common transitions are 0. This confirms that the a2 and S1 effects are about equal and add up (the recorded weights were -0.14 and -0.13).

Even the improved form leaves some reward x transition structure. Misses: D1 after a1 S2 r +0.086, a2 S1 r +0.070, a1 S1 u -0.099, a2 S2 u -0.066. The remaining errors look like a small reward-by-rare-transition interaction, below the last-trial ceiling of 0.68.

Other variants on test: replacing the two indicators with interaction terms scores 0.515. Scaling the terms by ep_dec drops to 0.42. Using in_rew instead of prev_reward gives the same 0.517. Adding belief_lo instead of a third term gives 0.49. Belief explains little (reference 0.17). There is no future-variable issue.
